newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian tobacco factory to make Winston, Camel.
newsitem.headline: Serbian tobacco factory to make Winston, Camel.

text.p: The Vranje tobacco industry Duvanska Industrija Vranje (DIV) will resume production of Winston and Camel under licence from the U.S. firm RJ Reynolds, state news agency Tanjug reported Monday.

"DIV plans to start the production of cigarettes under the Reynolds licence -- Winston by the end of November and Camel in early 1997," Slavoljub Vuckovic, DIV acting general manager, was quoted by Tanjug as saying.
DIV produced Winston and Camel cigarettes until international sanctions were imposed on Yugoslavia in May 1992.
"Since Winston licenced cigarettes are manufactured from a tobacco mix especially prepared by Reynolds, the raw material has arrived from the United States and production can begin," Vuckovic said.
Vuckovic announced plans for DIV to begin production of Winchester cigarettes as well next year.

Yugoslav tobacco factories' total capacity is estimated at 20,000 tonnes a year but they have been running at barely 60 percent of that due to booming illegal cigarette trade. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +381 112224305
